texts.preamble: Shree Vardhman Parivar vs The State Of West Bengal And Others on 29 October, 2025 October 29, 2025 Sl. No.65 Court No.1 s.biswas Wpa(P) 427 of 2025 Shree Vardhman Parivar vs. The State of West Bengal and others Mr. Vinay Kr. Sharaff Mr. Dev Kr. Agarwal Ms. Swarnwarshi Poddar
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that this petition is filed to prevent illegal sacrifice of animals. By taking this court to a report (Annexure P-14) by a committee constituted by Supreme Court in WP(C) 881 of 2014, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the Chief Secretary of the State of West Bengal was also a party. Reliance is placed on Clause 5 of the said report which reads thus: "5) Restriction on slaughter: Apart from focusing on Gadhimai alone, which happens once in 5 years, all the small animal sacrifice events may also be summarily discouraged and illegal slaughter of animals prevented by the State Govts. and their agencies. This way a solid platform and precedence can be built before the next Gadhimai event. No animal slaughter may be allowed at any religious or public place and slaughter may be permitted only in accordance with the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 and Regulations 2011." 3. It is further submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the said report, pursuant to a joint meeting of the respondent State, was placed before the Supreme Court on 13.07.2015 in WP(C) Shree Vardhman Parivar vs The State Of West Bengal And Others on 29 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133374587/ 1 881 of 2014. Reliance is also placed on the order dated 04.07.2016 of Supreme Court in the case wherein State of West Bengal also submitted its affidavit. 4. The learned counsel for the petitioner by placing reliance on the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 2001 submits that animals cannot be slaughtered except in the manner prescribed in this Rules. By placing heavy reliance on Rule 3 of the said Rules, it is submitted that slaughter of animals is permissible only in the slaughter house recognized or licensed by the concerned authority empowered under the law. Sub-Rule 3 of Rule 3 further makes it clear that number of animals to be slaughtered in a day has to be determined by the concerned municipal/local authority. 5. In the instant case, the sacrifice of the animals at the puja pandals which runs contrary to the Rules of 2001. Such sacrifice is totally impermissible and runs contrary to the spirit of the orders of the Supreme Court and the statutory mandate engraved in the Rules of 2001. 6. Learned counsel for the State submits that the State has already formed a committee to ensure that illegal slaughter does not take place. 7. The State Government is directed to seek instruction whether animal sacrifice in case of this nature falls within the ambit of "prohibited practices" as defined in Rule 2(t) of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act.
